FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: steak au poivre
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a cut of {0_adj} pressed into cracked pepper before it is seared, the pan deglazed with cognac and mounted with {2_plur}. The pepper has to be crushed, never ground.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: entrecôte bordelaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} grilled over vine cuttings, napped with a reduction of red {1_adj} and shallot, with poached rounds of marrow laid over it at the last moment.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bavette with shallots
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} seared very fast and served rare — cooked any further it becomes uneatable — under {1_adj} melted down in {2_plur} and vinegar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tournedos Rossini
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a medallion of {0_adj} on a crouton, crowned with a fried escalope of {1_adj} and slivers of {2_adj}, the whole moistened with a madeira sauce. Attributed to the composer, who is said to have demanded it of his cook.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bœuf à la mode
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a cut of {0_adj} larded and barded, braised whole with {1_coll} and {2_coll} and a calf's foot that sets the juices to jelly once cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bœuf miroton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the {0_adj} left over from the pot-au-feu, sliced and reheated in a {1_adj} sauce with vinegar and mustard. A dish born of thrift and kept on for the taste of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tongue in sauce piquante
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached for hours then peeled while still hot — cold, the skin will not come away — served under a {1_adj} sauce with vinegar and gherkins.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tête de veau sauce gribiche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} rolled and poached in a white broth, served warm under a sauce built on hard-boiled {1_adj} yolks, lifted with capers and herbs. You either eat it or you do not; there is no middle ground.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tripes à la mode de Caen
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and an ox foot shut into a tripe pot sealed with pastry, with {1_coll} and {2_coll}, and left in the oven for ten hours.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tablier de sapeur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a piece of {0_adj} marinated in white wine, crumbed with {1_plur} and breadcrumbs, then grilled. The name comes from a marshal of Lyon who had been a sapper in his youth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pieds et paquets
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: squares of {0_adj} stuffed with {2_plur}, garlic and parsley, sewn shut one by one, and stewed in {1_plur} with lamb's trotters. Marseille and Sisteron each claim it as their own.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kidneys in mustard
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} trimmed of its fat, sliced and seared over a high flame for a few seconds only, the sauce bound with {1_plur} and {2_plur} off the heat — boiled mustard turns bitter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: calf's liver with parsley
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a slice of {0_adj} fried in {2_plur} cooked to hazelnut, one minute a side, then thrown into finely chopped {1_plur} and parsley.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sweetbreads with morels
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} soaked out, blanched, pressed under a weight overnight, then gilded in butter and served with {1_coll} and a {2_adj} sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: andouillette and chips
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an andouillette grilled until the skin splits open, with {1_coll} in batons and a spoonful of mustard. You either love it or you leave the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: salt pork with lentils
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} salted in coarse salt and then soaked out overnight, stewed with {1_coll} and {2_coll}. The lentils are never salted before the end, or they stay hard.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: palette à la diable
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: smoked {0_coll} poached, painted over with {1_plur} and breadcrumbs, then run under the grill until it crusts. À la diable means only this: mustarded and scalding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ham à la chablisienne
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thick slices of {0_adj} napped with a reduction of white {1_adj} and shallot, mounted with {2_plur}, then glazed under the grill.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: roast bird
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole bird rubbed with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, roasted turned onto each thigh in turn before it finishes on its back. The juice that runs from the carcass at carving is worth any sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poulet basquaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} gilded then stewed in a fondue of {1_adj} and {2_adj} lifted with Espelette pepper, which bites just enough to be noticed.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chicken chasseur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fried and then stewed with {1_plur}, {2_plur} and tarragon, in a sauce deglazed with white wine.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chicken with tarragon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached in white wine, the sauce reduced and bound with {1_plur}, scented with {2_plur} added in two goes: during the cooking, then raw at the end.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poulet vallée d'Auge
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} flamed with calvados, stewed in cider with {1_coll} taken in butter, the sauce finished with thick {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coq au riesling
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Alsatian version, in white wine: {0_coll} stewed in dry {1_plur}, the sauce bound with {2_plur}. Served with noodles, never with potatoes.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: duck à l'orange
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} roasted and served under a bigarade sauce: a {2_adj} caramel slaked with vinegar, let down with the juice of bitter {1_adj} and the roasting juices.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: duck with turnips
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with {1_coll} glazed in the rendered fat and whole {2_coll}. The turnip drinks up the fat of the duck: that is the whole pairing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: duck with olives
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in a {2_adj} stock, with {1_coll} blanched to draw out their salt before they go in.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} navarin
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} seared then dusted with a little flour, braised with {1_coll} and {2_coll} cut into cloves. The name is said to come from the turnip, or from the battle — both versions circulate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: leg of {0_adj}
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole leg stuck with {1_plur} and roasted, basted with {2_plur} every ten minutes. It is carved parallel to the bone, in fine slices.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: seven-hour lamb
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a shoulder cooked so long and so gently in {1_plur} and {2_plur} that it can be eaten with a spoon. It is also called lamb à la cuiller, for exactly that reason.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} civet
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated and then braised in {1_plur}, the sauce bound with the animal's own blood off the heat. That is what parts a civet from a plain stew.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rabbit with prunes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in {2_plur} with dried {1_coll} swollen back up in water, which fall apart at the end of the cooking and sweeten the sauce by themselves.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_coll} grand veneur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a piece of game served under a poivrade mounted with {2_plur} and softened with a spoonful of {1_adj} jelly. The sauce of the grand veneur, the officer charged with the royal hunts.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: quail with grapes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small birds barded and roasted fast, deglazed with verjuice, with {1_coll} peeled and warmed through in {2_plur} just before serving.
